summary: Libyan security forces continue a violent crackdown on anti-government protests, with witnesses reporting dozens killed in Benghazi and Misratah as demonstrators vow further rallies demanding Muammar Gadhafi's departure.

Saif al-Islam Gaddafi promised a program of reforms after protests against Muammar Gaddafi's rule reached the capital, acknowledged that police and army made mistakes in dealing with protests, and said the General People's Congress would convene to discuss a reform agenda.
Violent unrest against Muammar Gaddafi's rule spread to the capital Tripoli, with police using tear gas and gunfire heard, after scores of protesters were killed in the east of Libya.
The U.N. Security Council schedules a Tuesday morning meeting on Libya at the request of Libya's deputy ambassador to the United Nations, who called the crackdown in Libya a "genocide."

Anti-government protesters rallied in Tripoli for the first time and a major government building was set on fire, as Saif al-Islam Gaddafi warned of civil war and said the regime would fight "to the last man standing."
Libya experts say the country faces likely chaos and possible bloodshed as Muammar Gaddafi's 42-year rule appears to be in an endgame, though his departure is not certain.
International leaders condemn the Libyan government's violent crackdown on protesters, with the UK summoning the Libyan ambassador and calling for an immediate end to the violence.
Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi makes a brief television appearance to deny reports that he had fled the country amid a spreading revolt .

A Libyan pilot and co-pilot reportedly refused orders to bomb oil fields southwest of Benghazi and ejected from their plane, which then crashed, amid growing international and domestic opposition to Moammar Gadhafi's crackdown on anti-government protesters.
Libyans celebrated the liberation of eastern Libya from Muammar Gaddafi's rule as Gaddafi vowed to crush the revolt and sought to assert his grip on Tripoli.
Al Qaeda's North African wing, Al Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb, said it will do whatever it can to help the uprising in Libya, according to a statement posted on jihadist websites.
Libya's former justice minister Mustafa Mohamed Abud Ajleil has led the formation of an interim government based in the eastern city of Benghazi, according to Libya's Quryna newspaper.
Saif al-Islam Gaddafi says the unrest in Libya has opened the door to all options, including civil war and foreign intervention.
The United States says Libya could descend into civil war unless Muammar Gaddafi quits, as Gaddafi remains defiant and Western military preparations are reported.
French Foreign Minister Alain Juppe says no military intervention in Libya is planned and that any intervention would require a clear UN Security Council mandate.
Libyan rebels repulsed a land and air offensive by Muammar Gaddafi's forces on Brega, as Gaddafi warned foreign powers of "another Vietnam" if they intervened.

President Obama said Moammar Gadhafi has lost legitimacy to lead and must leave, while authorizing U.S. military and civilian aircraft to help evacuate Egyptian citizens fleeing unrest in Libya and saying all options, including a no-fly zone, remain on the table.
Libyan rebels pushed west and extended their grip on a key coast road as Muammar Gaddafi received a warning he would be held to account at The Hague for suspected crimes by his security forces.
Fighting in Libya increasingly threatens oil infrastructure near coastal export hubs, raising the risk of long-term damage to the country's oil industry.

Muammar Gaddafi's forces fought their way into the rebel-held western town of Zawiyah, while rebels said they captured the eastern oil town of Ras Lanuf, and pro-Gaddafi forces bombed an arms depot on the outskirts of Benghazi.
Opposition forces in Misrata, Libya, repelled an onslaught by Moammar Gadhafi's troops and maintained control of the key city, with a doctor reporting at least 42 killed.
Troops loyal to Muammar Gaddafi launched counter-offensives against rebel-held towns in Libya, increasing fears that Libya is heading for a civil war.
Fierce battles raged for control of key Libyan cities as Libya entered its fourth week of fighting and continued its descent into civil war.
The International Committee of the Red Cross says Libya has descended into civil war with increasing numbers of wounded civilians arriving in hospitals in eastern cities .
The United States plans to send "purely humanitarian" disaster relief teams into eastern Libya, while National Intelligence Director James Clapper warns that Gadhafi is likely to survive the revolt.
Three Dutch marines detained in Libya were released and flown to Athens aboard a Greek military plane.

Forces loyal to Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi fired artillery into Ajdabiya and there were eyewitness reports of at least two airstrikes on the city, with Libyan state television reporting that Ajdabiya had been cleansed, while an opposition spokesman disputed the claim and said a small unit of government forces had entered the city but were repelled.
The U.N. Security Council approves a no-fly zone and permits "all necessary measures" to protect civilians in Libya.

An international military coalition including France, the United States and Great Britain attacked Libyan air-defense and other military targets, in an operation that eventually will include enforcing a no-fly zone.
A fighter jet was shot down and exploded in the Benghazi area of Libya amid ongoing clashes between rebel forces and pro-Gadhafi troops.
President Obama authorizes U.S. military intervention in Libya, a quite different operation from the 2003 invasion of Iraq.

A U.S. general says attacks on Libya are likely to slow in the coming days as Western powers consolidate a no-fly zone, while rebels have done little to capitalize on the bombardment and Washington rules out specific action to overthrow Gaddafi.
China said that Western air strikes on Libya risked a "humanitarian disaster," adding to criticism from major emerging powers over the U.N.-authorized campaign.

U.S. President Barack Obama said the United States will be able to hand over control of the coalition mission in Libya in days, as fighting continued in Misrata and Muammar Gadhafi vowed to emerge victorious.
Coalition airstrikes against Libyan government forces continued for a sixth day, striking the Tripoli suburb of Tajura as loyalist troops attacked the rebel-held city of Misrata.
Western warplanes bombed Muammar Gaddafi's tanks and artillery in eastern Libya to try to break a battlefield stalemate and help rebels take the strategic town of Ajdabiyah.
Rebel forces took control of the key eastern Libyan city of Ajdabiya overnight and advanced west toward Brega and Tripoli as coalition airstrikes continued against Gadhafi's forces.
Libyan Foreign Minister Moussa Koussa resigns and travels to London, according to the U.K. government.
Libyan rebels retreated east, ceding land and oil towns to Muammar Gaddafi's forces after they unleashed rockets and artillery on the lightly armed rebel forces.
Jordan sent fighter aircraft to a European air base to support a no-fly zone over Libya and protect humanitarian flights, according to Foreign Minister Nasser Judeh.
Forces loyal to Muammar Gaddafi are accused of staging a "massacre" in the besieged city of Misrata, as Turkey seeks to broker a ceasefire.
NATO says Western air strikes have destroyed nearly a third of Muammar Gaddafi's military since last month, but it has changed bombing tactics because Gaddafi forces are using human shields.
The head of Libya's rebel army condemns NATO for its slow chain of command in ordering air strikes to protect civilians, saying the alliance is letting the people of Misrata die every day.
A U.S. envoy arrived in Benghazi to get to know Libya's opposition and discuss how the United States might help meet its financial needs.

Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi urges U.S. President Barack Obama to end the NATO bombing of Libya in a letter, while Secretary of State Hillary Clinton says the strikes will stop when Gadhafi steps down and leaves the country .

Eman al-Obeidy, the Libyan woman who says forces loyal to Moammar Gadhafi raped her, remains unable to leave Tripoli and faces abuse whenever she leaves her house, as Human Rights Watch calls for Libyan authorities to allow her to leave and receive medical care.

A top U.S. general says a stalemate appears to be emerging in Libya between rebels and forces loyal to Muammar Gaddafi, and that the United States should not decide to arm the rebels without knowing more about them.

In Tripoli, children were bused to a square outside a UN office and told to chant anti-Western slogans amid apparent NATO air strikes, while some Libyans expressed dissent and said it was time for Muammar Gaddafi to go.
Rebels said five of their fighters were killed when NATO planes mistakenly bombed a rebel tank column near the contested port of Brega in eastern Libya, and NATO said it was investigating the attack.
Libya says a U.N.-mandated British air strike hit its major Sarir oilfield, killing three guards and damaging a pipeline connecting the field to a Mediterranean port.
Brent crude jumped to a 32-month high above $125 as attacks on Libyan oil fields made long-term supply cuts more likely.

Embattled Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi , in negotiations with the African Union , has agreed in principal to a deal that would end the conflict in the nation he 's ruled for 42 years , South African President Jacob Zuma told reporters Sunday .

The United States reacted cautiously to an African Union peace plan for Libya that was rejected by rebels, with Secretary of State Hillary Clinton saying Washington was waiting for details and not clarifying whether the proposal required Muammar Gaddafi to step down.

Hopes for a Libyan cease-fire were raised briefly when it was announced that Moammar Gadhafi had agreed, in principle, to the African Union's "road map" proposal for peace, though his opposition later rejected the proposal.
Libyan rebels scrambled to defend the eastern frontline outpost of Ajdabiyah after fighting with Muammar Gaddafi's troops on the coastal highway toward the oil port of Brega.
Britain says it will send about a dozen military officers to advise Libyan rebels, while denying it will arm or train them to fight or conduct a ground invasion.

The United Nations said the Libyan government's reported use of cluster munitions and heavy weapons in Misrata has caused substantial civilian casualties and may amount to crimes under international law.
A NATO airstrike on Misrata killed 11 rebel fighters and wounded two others, according to witnesses, while NATO spokesman Eric Povel said he knew nothing about the report.
Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi survived a NATO air strike on a Tripoli house that killed his youngest son and three grandchildren, according to a government spokesman.

Libya said Muammar Gaddafi's youngest son and three grandchildren were killed in a NATO air strike, though the deaths have not been independently confirmed and NATO denied targeting Gaddafi or his family.
Sudan deployed troops at the Libyan border to prevent arms smuggling to Darfur rebels and closed the Libyan consulate in al-Fasher after Libya closed Sudan's consulate in al-Kufrah.
Four rockets struck the compound belonging to Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi in Tripoli, according to a Libyan government official.
More than 400 people fleeing Libya and Tunisia arrived overnight on the Italian island of Lampedusa, including 199 people fleeing Libya's civil war.

The chairman of Libya's National Oil Corporation, Shokri Ghanem, reportedly defected from Muammar Gaddafi's administration and fled to neighboring Tunisia, though a Tripoli government official said there was no sign he had defected.

The European Union is considering tightening sanctions on Muammar Gaddafi's government by blacklisting Libyan ports to prevent oil exports and fuel imports, with proposals possibly submitted to the EU sanctions committee next week.
Jordan recognizes Libya's Interim National Council as the legitimate representative of the Libyan people and will send a permanent envoy to Benghazi.

Explosions erupted in Tripoli for a second consecutive night as NATO jets struck a vocational secondary school, according to a Libyan government official, while the U.S. acknowledged providing munitions to allies in the Libya air campaign and Obama warned Gadhafi there would be no letup in airstrikes.
NATO used attack helicopters for the first time in its military operation aimed at increasing pressure on Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi's regime.
China made its first confirmed contact with Libyan rebels, meeting with the National Transitional Council chairman in Qatar, in a diplomatic setback for Muammar Gaddafi.
A Russian envoy visited rebel-held Benghazi and said Moscow wanted to help bridge the rift in Libya by acting as a mediator in the conflict.

Qatar has provided hundreds of millions of dollars in fuel, food, medicine, and cash transfers to Libyan rebels in Benghazi, and is believed to have supplied arms, in support of the uprising against Muammar Gaddafi.
Western and Arab nations meet in Abu Dhabi to focus on the "end-game" for Libya's Muammar Gaddafi as NATO steps up air raids on Tripoli.

NATO aircraft have repeatedly bombed presidential compounds in Tripoli, Libya, as a CNN source says NATO believes the U.N. resolution on Libya justifies killing Moammar Gadhafi, while NATO denies targeting individuals.

Heavy fighting between pro-Gaddafi troops and rebels broke out in the Libyan city of Zlitan, potentially opening the coastal road to Tripoli, as Gaddafi forces also shelled the world heritage-listed city of Gadamis for the first time.

The Libyan government said 19 civilians were killed in a NATO air strike on the home of a top Gaddafi official in Surman, while NATO said it bombed a legitimate military command and control node and could not confirm civilian casualties.

Two influential U.S. senators introduce a resolution expressing support for limited American involvement in the NATO-led military campaign in Libya, while House Speaker John Boehner proposes two resolutions on the Libya mission that could come up for votes on Thursday.
A French minister says it is time for Libya's rebels to negotiate with Muammar Gaddafi's government, while Washington says it stands firm in its belief that the Libyan leader cannot stay in power .

Western powers and Arab states meet in Istanbul to seek a political solution to end the civil war in Libya, amid conflicting signals over whether Muammar Gaddafi intends to fight on or surrender power.
The United States recognizes the Transitional National Council as the legitimate governing authority for Libya.
Russia criticizes the United States and other countries for recognizing Libya's rebel National Transitional Council as the legitimate government, saying they are taking sides in the civil war.
The Libyan government in Tripoli estimates the five-month conflict has cost the national economy some $50 billion, with suspended oil and gas exports accounting for about $20 billion of the losses.
Libyan government spokesman Moussa Ibrahim says Libyan representatives are ready to hold more talks with the United States and with rebels, but Muammar Gaddafi will not bow to demands he leave power.
The U.N. envoy to Libya and the Benghazi-based rebel council discussed ideas for ending the civil war, but no firm initiative had yet taken shape.
British Foreign Secretary William Hague says Moammar Gadhafi must leave power but leaves Gadhafi's fate beyond that open to question, saying it is ultimately for Libyans to determine.
U.N. special envoy Abdul Elah al-Khatib travels to Tripoli to seek a political process to end the civil war, as Western powers signal Muammar Gaddafi could stay in Libya if he gives up power.

Britain recognized the rebel National Transitional Council as Libya's legitimate government and expelled Gaddafi's diplomats from London, while the rebels withdrew their offer to allow Gaddafi to stay in Libya if he gave up power.
Libyan rebel army commander General Abdul Fatah Younis was killed along with two senior officers, with the circumstances and perpetrators unknown.

Libyan rebel military chief Abdel Fattah Younes was killed by allied militiamen, according to rebel minister Ali Tarhouni, who said a militiaman had been arrested and confessed that his subordinates had carried out the killing.

The U.S. prepares to hand over the Libyan embassy in Washington to the rebel Transitional National Council while warning the TNC to investigate the assassination of its military commander, Abdel Fatah Younis, amid internal divisions.
Libyan rebels said they launched a push to capture the coastal oil town of Brega, advancing slowly because Muammar Gaddafi's forces had sown minefields across its approaches.

Libyan Transitional National Council Chairman Mustafa Abdel Jalil dismissed the rebels' 14-member executive board, with a spokesman saying the death of military commander Gen. Abdel Fattah Younis played a role.
Rebel forces in western Libya advanced north toward Zawiyah, coming within 25 km of the town and less than 50 km from Tripoli, as they tried to get within striking range of the capital.

Libyan rebels pushed northward on three fronts toward the coastal cities of al-Zawiya, Aziziya and Sorman, aiming ultimately for Tripoli, as the Libyan Embassy in Washington reopened under the control of the Transitional National Council.
Troops loyal to Muammar Gaddafi remain in control of the oil terminal and refinery in the strategic eastern port of Brega despite rebel advances, according to a rebel spokesman.
Forces loyal to Muammar Gaddafi fired a Scud missile for the first time in the Libyan civil war, according to a U.S. defense official.
NATO says anti-Gadhafi rebel forces are taking control of the key approaches to Tripoli, described as the most significant anti-Gadhafi territorial gain in months.
Libya's rebel National Transitional Council denies holding any direct or indirect talks with Muammar Gaddafi's government or with the U.N. special envoy for Libya to resolve the civil war.
Libyan rebels fought forces loyal to Muammar Gaddafi for control of oil facilities in Zawiyah and Brega, with a rebel spokesman saying a pipeline to Tripoli was cut.
Libyan officials reject rebel claims that Moammar Gadhafi is seeking refuge for his family, saying the leader and his wife and children do not plan to leave the country.
Libyan rebels launched Operation Dawn Mermaid, a coordinated assault on Tripoli involving secret rebel units inside the capital and NATO airstrikes, leading to the rebels' entry into the city.
Libyan rebel fighters enter Tripoli with little resistance, reaching Green Square and detaining two of Muammar Gaddafi's sons.
Rebel fighters took Muammar Gaddafi's compound in central Tripoli amid intense gun battles.
Libya faces a difficult decade-long transition toward democracy after Gaddafi's fall, requiring security, state-building, and international support.

Libyan rebels claimed to be close to capturing Muammar Gaddafi as their NATO backers bombed loyalists in his tribal bastion, while the African Union refused to recognize the National Transitional Council as the legal government.

Libyan rebel forces converged on Muammar Gaddafi's hometown of Sirte, hoping to seize it by force if negotiations for its surrender failed, while Gaddafi's whereabouts remained unknown five days after Tripoli fell.
Libya plans to restart production at two eastern oil fields in mid-September and resume shipping oil from Tobruk by the end of September.
Algeria is to close the southern part of its border with Libya, according to a local newspaper report, the day after Algeria gave safe haven to members of Muammar Gaddafi's family.
Libya's interim leadership rejects the idea of deploying any kind of international military force or observers, according to the U.N. special envoy on post-conflict planning for Libya.
Russia recognizes Libya's National Transitional Council as the country's legitimate authority.

Libya's National Transitional Council reaffirmed its commitment to democracy and planned spending of billions of dollars released from frozen Gaddafi assets after international powers agreed to hand over more than $15 billion.
The European Union lifted sanctions on Libyan ports, oil firms and banks as foreign ministers met to discuss helping the country's transition from Muammar Gaddafi's rule.
Muammar Gaddafi was last tracked heading for Libya's southern border, according to the man leading the hunt, though Burkina Faso denied any plan to offer him refuge.

Muammar Gaddafi vows to fight on from hiding, denying he fled Libya and calling his opponents rats and stray dogs, as Libyan interim authorities struggle to impose authority and extend a truce until Saturday for negotiated surrenders at Bani Walid and Sirte .
Fighters loyal to Libya's new rulers launched assaults on the final bastions of Muammar Gaddafi loyalists, with fighting reported inside Bani Walid and near Gaddafi's home town of Sirte.

Libya's new rulers said their fighters were holding back an assault on Bani Walid, one of the last bastions loyal to Muammar Gaddafi, after finding civilians in peril, while Niger reported that Saadi Gaddafi had crossed into its territory.
Britain circulates a draft UN Security Council resolution to ease sanctions against Libya, aiming to unfreeze assets for the National Oil Corp and central bank and enable them to function.
Libya's interim government said its forces had seized the airport and fort in Sabha, one of the last strongholds of forces loyal to Muammar Gaddafi.
Libya's interim rulers say they have captured most of Sabha, which had been holding out, as well as Bani Walid and Sirte since the fall of the capital Tripoli.

Tunisia jails Muammar Gaddafi's former prime minister Al Baghdadi Ali al-Mahmoudi for illegally entering the country, as Libya's new rulers tighten their grip on desert towns where Gaddafi may be hiding.
Suncor Energy says it is still unwilling to send employees back to Libya even though its joint-venture partner Harouge Oil Operations is preparing to resume oil production.

Intense sniper and artillery fire from forces loyal to Muammar Gaddafi in Sirte kept fighters with Libya's interim National Transitional Council at bay, as NTC forces encircled the city and NATO conducted aerial attacks.
Displaced residents of Tawargha, Libya, shelter near Sirte, fearing reprisal attacks by anti-Gaddafi fighters from Misrata who accuse them of supporting Muammar Gaddafi.
People wounded in fighting in Libya's besieged city of Sirte are dying on the operating table because fuel for the hospital generator has run out, medical workers fleeing the city said.
Libyan transitional government forces said they had cornered Muammar Gaddafi loyalists in the center of Sirte, Gaddafi's hometown, where street fighting continued and civilians were trying to flee.
Fighters loyal to Muammar Gaddafi fought a last-ditch battle in an ever shrinking pocket of resistance in the ousted leader's hometown Sirte .

Secretary of State Hillary Clinton made an unannounced visit to Libya to cement relations with the new leaders Washington helped install , offer aid and encourage them to follow through on a promise of swift elections .
Libyan interim government fighters renewed their offensive on the besieged town of Sirte after being pushed back by Muammar Gaddafi loyalists.
Muammar Gaddafi was captured and killed near his home town of Sirte, with conflicting accounts of whether he died from wounds sustained during capture or was beaten and shot by fighters.
NTC fighters capture Sirte, Gaddafi's hometown, ending a two-month siege and extinguishing the last significant holdout of troops loyal to the deposed leader.
